Please solve this issue:

## Bug Description

The Sensor Async Read API (sensor_read_async_mempool) is documented as asynchronous and non-blocking, but the execution path is synchronous for most (if not all) in-tree driver implementations. The sensor driver submit callbacks block on the calling thread, making the API unsuitable for time-sensitive contexts.

Examples of synchronous behavior in current drivers:
  - ICM42688 RTIO driver: submit callback performs I2C/SPI transactions synchronously
  - AKM09918C async driver: blocks on bus read in submit path
  - BMA4XX sensor driver: synchronous channel fetch in submit
  - BME280 async driver: synchronous bus read in submit

The solution is to decouple the sensor read request from its execution by introducing an RTIO Work-queues service. This service uses a priority-aware work queue pool (P4WQ) with pre-allocated work items to process sensor requests asynchronously on dedicated threads.

Required changes:
1. Create the RTIO work-queue service: a new header (include/zephyr/rtio/work.h), Kconfig options (CONFIG_RTIO_WORKQ, CONFIG_RTIO_WORKQ_THREADS_POOL, CONFIG_RTIO_WORKQ_PRIO_MED), and implementation (subsys/rtio/rtio_workq.c)
2. Update the default RTIO sensor fallback (drivers/sensor/default_rtio_sensor.c) to use the work queue
3. Update individual sensor drivers (akm09918c, bma4xx, bme280, icm42688) to use rtio_work_req_alloc() and rtio_work_req_submit() in their submit callbacks
4. Add necessary Kconfig dependencies in driver and subsys Kconfig files
5. Update the sensor header (include/zephyr/drivers/sensor.h) for RTIO semaphore enablement

See: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/73676

function.arguments:
{"command": "
echo "# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

config RTIO_WORKQ
	bool \"RTIO Workqueue service\"
	default n
	help
	  Enable the RTIO workqueue service. This service provides a priority-aware
	  work queue pool (P4WQ) with pre-allocated work items to process sensor
	  requests asynchronously on dedicated threads.

config RTIO_WORKQ_THREADS_POOL
	int \"Number of threads in the RTIO workqueue pool\"
	default 2
	depends on RTIO_WORKQ
	range 1 8
	help
	  This option sets the number of threads that will be created for the
	  RTIO workqueue. These threads will process the sensor requests.

config RTIO_WORKQ_STACK_SIZE
	int \"Stack size for RTIO workqueue threads\"
	default 1024
	depends on RTIO_WORKQ
	help
	  This option sets the stack size for each thread in the RTIO workqueue pool.

config RTIO_WORKQ_PRIO_MED
	int \"Medium priority for RTIO workqueue threads\"
	default 8
	depends on RTIO_WORKQ
	help
	  This option sets the medium priority for the RTIO workqueue threads.

config RTIO_WORKQ_LOG_LEVEL
	int \"RTIO Workqueue log level\"
	default 0
	range 0 4
	depends on RTIO_WORKQ
	help
	  This option sets the log level for the RTIO workqueue service.
" > subsys/rtio/Kconfig.workq && \
echo "source \"subsys/rtio/Kconfig.workq\"" >> subsys/rtio/Kconfig && \
echo "zephyr_library(
  SOURCES
    rtio.c
  # Always present even if RTIO is disabled
  # Needed for drivers and other modules that always build
  # and link to get access to rtio_is_enabled()
  # and other APIs that may or may not be stubbed out.
  # Always make sure that the subsys/rtio/Kconfig is updated to reflect this.
)

if(CONFIG_RTIO_WORKQ)
  zephyr_library_append_sources(rtio rtio_workq.c)
endif()" > subsys/rtio/rtio.CMakeLists.txt_new && \
mv subsys/rtio/rtio.CMakeLists.txt_new subsys/rtio/CMakeLists.txt
"}
